生成された動画：=== CHARACTER LOCK — STRICT ===

YASUO:
Use the provided Yasuo reference to preserve his exact facial identity, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing design, sword design, and overall silhouette.

This scene takes place years earlier, so Yasuo should appear slightly younger, cleaner, healthier, and less worn than his later fugitive version while remaining unmistakably the same person.

Yasuo voice:
young adult male baritone, low and slightly rough, subtle natural rasp, confident and energetic but restrained.
Natural live-action delivery.
Do not make the voice theatrical or exaggerated.


YONE:
Use the provided Yone reference to preserve his exact facial identity, long dark hair, red-and-black Ionian clothing, body proportions, sword design, and calm disciplined presence.

Yone must remain visually and behaviorally distinct from Yasuo.

Yone voice:
deep smooth adult male baritone, calm, disciplined, controlled, speaking slowly with quiet authority.
Natural human delivery.
Never sound angry or theatrical in this scene.


YASUMASA:
Use the provided Yasumasa reference to preserve his exact identity, silver-gray tied hair, beard, facial structure, body proportions, clothing design, sword, and calm sword-master presence.

Do not make him weak, frail, theatrical, hurried, or aggressive.

His movements should be economical, balanced, precise, and highly controlled.

Yasumasa voice:
mature male baritone, deep, warm, steady, calm, deliberate, quietly authoritative.
He speaks slowly and naturally, never loudly unless necessary.


=== ENVIRONMENT LOCK ===

Use the provided Ionian mountain training courtyard reference as the primary environment.

Preserve the elevated mountain training courtyard, stone training floor, traditional temple architecture, shaded dojo interior, covered entrance, flowering trees, distant mountains, clouds, waterfalls, and peaceful atmosphere.

Natural daylight.
Soft mountain haze.
Gentle wind moving hair, robes, leaves, hanging fabric, and flower petals.

Keep the same environment, lighting direction, weather, and visual tone throughout the full video.


=== TECHNICAL ===

High-end live-action cinematic realistic fantasy.

16:9 cinematic widescreen.

Realistic human anatomy.
Natural human movement.
Realistic cloth and hair physics.
Grounded martial arts movement.
Realistic body mechanics.
Feature-film quality.

Maintain strict facial identity, costume, hairstyle, sword, and body proportion consistency throughout the video.

Use natural cinematic camera movement.

Keep the sequence simple, readable, and coherent.

Do not create excessive cuts.
Do not create rapid montage.
Do not introduce unrelated camera angles.
Do not add extra characters.
Do not add extra dialogue.
Do not add extra actions.
Do not add supernatural visual effects.
Do not make Yasumasa fly, teleport, sprint, or run hurriedly.

No subtitles.
No captions.
No visible text.
No watermark.
No logo.

Audio:
soft mountain wind,
birds,
subtle movement of leaves and flower petals,
quiet temple ambience,
natural footsteps on wood and stone,
subtle clothing movement.

No background music.

Dialogue must come only from the correct character.
Accurate natural lip synchronization.


=== CONTEXT FROM THE PREVIOUS VIDEO ===

This scene continues directly from the previous moment in the same training courtyard.

In the previous video, young Yasuo defeated a sparring partner with speed, strength, and confidence. After the sparring ended, Yasuo lowered his sword with a small satisfied smile while Yone watched calmly nearby.

The conversation now continues immediately after that victory, in the same place, with the same characters, the same clothing, the same daylight, and the same emotional continuity.


=== GLOBAL ACTION ===

Yone calmly reminds Yasuo that their master never told him that he had to win. Yasuo responds with youthful confidence and asks what their master actually told him to do.

A short silence follows.

Then Yasumasa’s calm voice is heard from inside the temple building behind them.

Yasuo reacts to the voice.

The camera quickly redirects toward the dojo interior and reveals Yasumasa seated calmly inside the shaded temple space, already listening to the conversation.

After a brief still moment, Yasumasa rises from the seated position in one smooth, controlled movement.

He does not run.

He walks toward the dojo entrance with calm, deliberate steps.

The camera creates the sense of momentum through a fast but controlled move toward the doorway.

As Yasumasa reaches the threshold, use a clean cinematic cut to compress the travel distance.

Do not show him running down the full set of stairs.

Cut to an exterior angle as one foot steps down onto the stone courtyard.

Yasumasa descends with controlled precision and continues forward at a calm walking pace.

The speed of the scene should come from editing and camera movement, not from Yasumasa moving hurriedly.

He arrives several steps in front of Yasuo, stops, becomes completely still, looks directly at him, and calmly tells him to come forward.

Yasuo’s youthful confidence shifts into focused respect, and he begins walking toward his master.

Emotional progression:
quiet disagreement → curiosity → unseen authority → reveal → controlled movement → stillness → respect.


=== BEAT 1 — YONE AND YASUO ===

Start with a close-up of Yone.

Yone looks directly at Yasuo with calm older-brother authority.

His expression is controlled and serious, but not angry.

Yone says naturally:

"Master never told you that you had to win."

Hold briefly on Yone after the line.

Then cut to a close-up of Yasuo.

Yasuo looks back at Yone with youthful confidence and slight curiosity.

Yasuo says:

"Then what did he tell me to do?"

Hold a brief natural silence after Yasuo finishes speaking.

Do not continue the conversation between Yasuo and Yone.


=== BEAT 2 — YASUMASA REVEAL ===

While staying close on Yasuo, a calm male voice is heard from inside the temple building behind him.

Yasumasa says off-screen:

"Learn how not to need to win."

Do not reveal Yasumasa before he speaks.

Let the voice arrive first.

Yasuo’s expression changes subtly from confidence to attention.

He looks toward the source of the voice.

Then the camera makes one fast but controlled directional move toward the dojo interior.

Reveal Yasumasa seated calmly inside the shaded temple space.

He has clearly been listening to the conversation.

Yasumasa sits with perfect posture and complete stillness.

His sword rests naturally beside him.

He does not look surprised.
He does not smile dramatically.
He does not pose.

He appears completely calm and in control.

Hold this reveal for a brief moment.


=== BEAT 3 — YASUMASA ENTERS THE COURTYARD ===

Yasumasa rises from the seated position in one smooth, efficient movement.

He does not run.

He walks toward the dojo entrance with calm, deliberate steps.

The camera moves quickly with him, creating forward momentum while Yasumasa himself remains composed.

As he reaches the doorway, use a clean cinematic cut.

Do not show the entire journey from the dojo interior to the courtyard.

Do not show him running down the stairs.

Cut directly to a lower exterior angle as Yasumasa places one foot onto the stone courtyard.

His descent should be precise, balanced, and controlled.

He continues forward at a calm walking pace.

The edit and camera movement should compress the distance and make his entrance feel efficient without making him hurried.

Yasumasa stops several steps in front of Yasuo.

The moment he stops, he becomes completely still and balanced.

He looks directly at Yasuo and says calmly:

"Come here."

His voice remains low, warm, steady, and effortless.

No anger.
No challenge.
No raised voice.

Yasuo’s earlier confidence fades into focused attention.

He begins walking toward Yasumasa.

Yone remains behind, quietly observing.

End the video before the sword lesson begins.


=== END STATE FOR CONTINUITY ===

Yasumasa is standing calmly in the training courtyard.

Yasuo is approaching him with focused attention.

Yone remains behind, quietly observing.

Do not begin the sword lesson yet.

The next video begins with Yasuo and Yasumasa facing each other before the lesson.


=== MOOD ===

The scene should establish Yasumasa’s authority through calm control.

He does not need to move quickly to feel powerful.

The camera and editing create the momentum, while Yasumasa remains composed, precise, and unhurried.

His presence should feel powerful without aggression or spectacle.

Yasuo should immediately understand that his master’s control is on a different level from his own youthful strength.、16:9
